name: German high gain (EL34, tight)
notes: 90s German high-gain style: very tight and precise low end, aggressive upper mids, EL34 power amp. Built from the general layout of such amps, NOT from one schematic: treat every value as approximate. Key ideas: a strong bass cut before the first clipping stage and smaller coupling caps between stages (very tight palm mutes), four cascaded 12AX7 stages, a mid-focused tone stack setting, EL34 pair with fairly strong feedback (tight) and presence. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: everything, by design; feedback amount set for about 8 dB. Phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage). POWER SUPPLY: silicon rectifier and a big filter capacitor: a stiff, tight supply, as 60 ohm into 100 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.) COUPLING: every tube stage STARTS with its coupling capacitor into its grid resistor (coupling_nf, grid_ohms; default 22 nF into 1 Mohm = 7.2 Hz; power tubes 22 nF into 220k = 33 Hz), a 1st-order high-pass, and its bias shift recovers in C x R through that same capacitor (the guessed release times are gone). The small capacitors of tight stages (0.6-2 nF, from the old 80-250 Hz high-passes) recover in 1-2 ms: that is why tight amps use them. The output transformer's low end stays a post highpass1. The cathode follower is DC-coupled to v4's plate (coupling_nf 0) and drives the tone stack directly; the tone stack's capacitors block the DC. PREAMP SUPPLY: every gain stage (v1, v2, v3, v4, cathode_follower, pi) hangs on the same supply through decoupling filters (preamp_targets), so it sags too, about 100 ms behind (preamp_filter_ms: a GUESS; real amps have 10k-ish resistors and 10-50 uF capacitors per node). OUTPUT TRANSFORMER: the core of a 100 W amp's transformer, saturating on full-power notes below about 30 Hz (transformer_sat_hz: a GUESS from the amp's size, not measured): loud low notes lose bass and get odd harmonics. POWER TUBES: four (pairs 2) into half the load (1700 ohm), as in the 100 W originals: each tube works as in one pair, so the clipping is the same; the supply feeds twice the current, so it sags more (the supply values were guessed for one pair and are still GUESSES).
